paragraphs: Meachar shehattepilla hi bimqom haqqarebban, upoh haadam bimqom hammizbeach shebbo maqrib haqqarebbanot, laken tzarik lekavven bitpillato keneged bet hammiqdash ubet qodesh haqqodashim, sheshsham mizbeach banuy veoleh recha hannichocha lah' derek bet qadeshe haqqodashim sheshsham shaar hashshamayim, vehaynu im haya haadam omed lehitpallel bechutz laaretz yachazir panayv keneged eretz yisrael, shenneemar "veyitpallu eleka derek artzam" (melakim  ch, mch), vikavven gam ken keneged yerushalayim ubet hammiqdash ubet qodesh haqqodashim, veomed beeretz yisrael yachazir panayv keneged yerushalayim ubet hammiqdash ubet qodesh haqqodashim, haya omed birushalayim yachazir panayv lammiqdash, nimtzeu kol yisrael mitpallelim lemaqom echad dehaynu bet hammiqdash ubet qodesh haqqodashim sheshsham shaar hashshamayim shekkol haqqarebbanot hayu olim lerecha nichocha lah' mishsham. ulekak gam hattepillot shehem dugmat haqqarebbanot olim derek sham, ulekak niqra bet hammiqdash "talpiyyot"- tel shekkol piyyot ponim bo, umatzati katub etza toba lihyot leadam lemazkeret sheyyirshom al dap hassiddur shello qodem tepillat haamida milot ellu "yerushalayim ubet hammiqdash ubet qodesh haqqodashim" beotiyyot gedolot ad kan, vehu minhag tob ki lerob hatteradot tzarik haadam laasot mazkeret ukemo sheamar hakkatub "hatztzibi leka tziyyunim" (yirmeya l, k), vaapillu lemi sheddarko lehitpallel tepillat haamida beal peh toil lo ki azhara shamanu tob laadam lehitpallel hazzemirot veah"yotzer" mittok hassiddur bishbil hakkavvana, remez laddabar "amar im hasseper yashub machashabto" (ester t, kh), velaken meachar shettopes hassiddur beyado kesheqqam lehitpallel roeh tebot ellu veyizkor: veim haya mitpallel bebet hakkeneset sheshsham noda hatztzad hamkuvvan keneged eretz yisrael shetztzarik lehitpallel kenegdo, ak zeh haadam suma sheeno roeh, o sibba haya lo veamad letzad acher, ap al pi shekkebar hitchil lehitpallel tzarik adam haroeh oto lehaamido keneged tzad harauy, veap al pi shebbazeh oqer raglayv ki aqirat raglayv bilbad la chashib hepseq bitpilla, vela mibbaya im otah shaa hayu hatztzibbur mitpallelin letzad harauy deaz nireh zeh sheomed letzad acher keillu chas veshalom modeh lirshut acher, devadday tzarik min haddin lehachazir panayv letzad shehatztzibbur mitpallelin alayv, ella apillu im lo hayu tzibbur mitpallelin otah shaa, mikkol maqom kevan deomed bebet hakkeneset sheshsham nikkar hatztzad harauy lehitpallel mikkoach amidat aron haqqodesh vehahekol vehabbima tzarik lehachazir panayv, abal im zeh mitpallel lebaddo betok bayit sheen bo siman vehekker velo hayu acherim mitpallelin otah shaa en tzarik lehipsiqu betok tepillato kevan shekkebar hitchil, ken haaleti besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" veayyen ,minchat aharon" kelal tv ot b' shehebi dibre ha"ture zahab" uteshubat "yad eliyyahu" umah shekkatab hu al dabar zeh:

clarification.explanation: Since prayer stands in place of the sacrifice, and here the person serves as the altar, one must direct his prayer toward the Beit HaMikdash and the Holy of Holies, through which prayer ascends to heaven just as the sacrificial aromas used to ascend there. Therefore one who is outside the Land of Israel should turn his face toward the Land of Israel, and should also direct his heart toward Jerusalem, the Beit HaMikdash, and the Holy of Holies. One who is in the Land of Israel should direct his face toward Jerusalem and the Temple, and one who is in Jerusalem itself should direct his face toward the Temple. Thus it emerges that all of Israel, from wherever they are, pray in one direction - toward the Temple, and therefore the Temple is called "Talpiyot" (a mound to which all mouths turn). Good advice is cited: to write on the page of the prayer book, before the Amidah, the words "Jerusalem, the Beit HaMikdash, and the Holy of Holies" in large letters, so that a person will have a reminder - and this is also good for one accustomed to praying by heart. In general, it is good to pray from the prayer book (and not only by heart) in order to assist one's intent. Likewise, if a person is about to pray in the synagogue where the correct direction is known (for example, by the position of the Ark), but he erred and turned in the wrong direction - he must be turned to the correct direction even if he has already begun praying, because moving the feet alone is not considered an interruption in prayer. This is true especially if the whole congregation is praying in the correct direction, in which case he appears to be facing a different direction. But if a person is praying alone in a place with no indication of the correct direction (such as a private home without an Ark), and no others are praying there at the time - there is no need to interrupt him in the middle of his prayer.
takeaways: It is good to write on the prayer book the words "Jerusalem, the Beit HaMikdash, and the Holy of Holies," so as to remember to direct one's heart toward them in prayer.

If one sees a person praying in the wrong direction in the synagogue, he must be turned to the correct direction even if he has already begun praying, since that alone is not considered an interruption.

paragraphs: Im holek bammidbar veeno yakol lekavven haruchot kede sheyyachazir panayv keneged eretz yisrael, o sheholek bispina bayyam ubinhar meuqqam depaam nehpeket laddarom paam lammizrach paam latztzapon, hinneh zeh yaamod kepi mah sheyyizdammen lo vikavven bilbabo davqa leeretz yisrael virushalayim ubet hammiqdash ubet qodesh haqqodashim:

clarification.explanation: One who travels in the desert and cannot know exactly the directions in order to turn toward the Land of Israel, and likewise one who travels by ship on the sea or on a winding river where the direction constantly changes (now south, now east, now north) - should stand and pray in whatever direction he happens to be facing at that moment, and only in his heart should he direct his thought toward the Land of Israel, Jerusalem, the Beit HaMikdash, and the Holy of Holies.
takeaways: When the exact direction cannot be known (in the desert, on a ship), one prays facing whatever direction one is in, and the direction toward the Land of Israel is achieved through intent alone.

paragraphs: Lo yaamod al gab maqom gabohha shelosha tepachim im eno muqqap shelosha mechitztzot, o sheen bo arba ammot al arba ammot, umitzva min hammubchar apillu bepachot mishshelosha, vetzarik lachush shello laamod al dabar deepshar sheyyachaliq mishshum demitterid shemma yippol, vekol kayyotze bazeh vaapillu al lucha shemmitnadned beopen demitterid beh, veken im lobesh qbq"b (qabqabbe etz) demitterid lemi sheeno ragil bo, vekol kayyotze bazeh veayyen "chesed lealpayim" v"minchat aharon" kelal tv ot v ushear acharonim za"l, vetzarik lehazhir et haam baitztabba sheyyesh bebet hakkeneset sheen bah arba ammot al arba ammot, veen bah mechitztzot shello lehitpallel aleha vedabar zeh matzuy bebatte kenesiyyot poh irenu:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to stand and pray on a place three handbreadths high or more, unless it is surrounded by three partitions, or has an area of four cubits by four cubits (so that it is considered an independent place rather than an "elevation" separating one from the congregation). And as the more proper practice, it is good to be careful of this even if the height is less than three handbreadths. Likewise, one must be careful not to stand in a place liable to slip, since fear of falling distracts one's intent, and the same applies to a board that wobbles, and to one who wears wooden clogs [kabkabim] he is unaccustomed to and feels unsteady in. Anything that causes distraction of mind in this way should be avoided during prayer. The congregation must also be warned regarding the raised platform [itztaba] found in some synagogues, which does not measure four cubits by four cubits and has no partitions, that they should not pray upon it - and this is found in the synagogues in the city of Rabbi Yosef Chaim.
takeaways: One should not pray on a place higher than three handbreadths without partitions or a sufficient area, so as not to appear cut off from the congregation.
One should avoid praying in a place that presents a risk of slipping or falling, since this confuses one's intent.

paragraphs: Katab hallebush za"l besiman try"t seip ' shello yaamod al karim veyitpallel mishshum shennireh kemitgaeh ayyen sham, verauy lehizzaher bazeh:

clarification.explanation: The "Levush" wrote that one should not stand on cushions (soft pillows) during prayer, because this appears as arrogance and pride, and one should be careful to avoid it.
takeaways: One should not pray while standing on soft cushions, so that it not appear as an act of pride.

paragraphs: Lo yihyeh dabar chotzetz beno leben haqqir im oto dabar gabohha asara tepachim verachebbo arbaa tepachim, abal dabar qabua ketiba vekayyotze ap al pi sheenam qebuim bebinyan baqqarqa en chotzetzim mippene shehem asuyim liqbiut sham tamid, veken adam eno chotzetz, umikkol maqom heka deepshar tob shello yitpallel achore shum adam, veayyen "chesed lealpayim" siman tz ot tv"b:

clarification.explanation: There must be nothing separating between the one praying and the wall, if that thing is ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide. But a fixed object such as a wall cabinet or the like, even though it is not attached to the ground itself, is not considered a separation, because it stands there permanently. Likewise, another person standing in front of him is not considered a separation. Nevertheless, when possible, it is preferable not to pray directly behind another person.
takeaways: A large temporary object separating the one praying from the wall is forbidden, but fixed furniture or another person are not considered a separation - yet it is still preferable not to pray directly behind someone.

paragraphs: Asur lesheb betok arba ammot shel mitpallel tepillat haamida ben millepanayv ben millaachorayv ben min hatztzedadim, vechutz learba ammot shari, veyesh omerim lepanayv asur kimlo enayv, vehamminhag kisbara rishona, mihu im hayyosheb oseq bidbarim shehem mittiqqune hattepillot hen beparashat hattamid vehaqqetoret vaapillu pereq "ezehu meqoman" hen bizmirot hen biqriat shema ubirkoteha muttar lo lesheb, veap al pi sheyyesh machmirin beoseq beqarebbanot, veod yesh machmirin gam beoseq bizmirot yesh lismok bazeh al hammeqillin veshari gam beoseq beqarebbanot, abal im oseq battora lav, ubishat haddechaq utzerok gadol yesh lismok gam al hammattirin beoseq bedibre tora, lekak im en lo maqom lesheb chutz learba ammot, o shehu choleh veeno yakol laamod lehitracheq chutz learba ammot mechamat chulsha o sibba acheret hekrechit, yesh lehattir laasoq battora shello yihyeh yosheb vedomem ella yaasoq battora o yiqra ezeh mizmorim ad sheyyesayyem zeh tepillato: vaapillu im zeh hayyosheb kebar haya yosheb vehammitpallel ba bigbulo gam ken tzarik laqum abal im haya yosheb bemaqom sheeno maqom litpilla uba zeh bigbulo lehitpallel en tzarik laqum mishshurat haddin veraq ikka bazeh middat chasidut laqum. vehinneh poh irenu mizdammen shebbaim haqqahal shebbaim haqqahal bishat mincha lebet hakkalla kede laamod besheba berakot shemmebarekim sham bishat hachuppa veyesh bene adam shemmitpallelin bebet hakkeneset ubaim sham umotzein haqqahal shebbau lebet hakkalla mitpallelin tepillat haamida sham, velo yesh maqom lehitracheq umukrach sheyyesheb betzedam samuk lahem mammash veim yaamod velo yesheb choshesh leyuhara o sibba acheret shemmukrach lesheb, hinneh zeh yesh lo taqqana lilmod belachash petichat eliyyahu zakur lattob o ezeh mizmorim beal peh, velo yihyeh yosheb vedomem:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to sit within four cubits (about two meters) of one who is praying the Amidah, whether in front of him, behind him, or to his sides; outside of four cubits it is permitted. Some say that in front of him it is forbidden even at a greater distance ("as far as his eyes can see"), but the custom follows the first opinion. Nevertheless, if the one sitting is engaged in matters of prayer - such as the passage "Eizehu Mekoman," the recitation of the Tamid offering and incense passages, Pesukei DeZimra, the Shema and its blessings - he is permitted to sit, even though some are stringent about this. But if he is engaged in Torah study, one should not be lenient, except in a time of pressing need. Therefore, one who has no place to sit outside the four cubits, or an ill person who cannot stand at a distance, is permitted to engage in Torah study or recite Psalms, so that he not sit idle. Even if the one sitting was already sitting in his place before the one praying came to stand within his boundary, the one sitting must still rise; but if the one sitting was sitting in a place not designated for prayer, and the one praying came there to pray, there is no obligation for the one sitting to rise as a matter of strict law - only as a measure of piety. Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes a local custom: when the congregation arrives at the time of Mincha at the house of the bride for the Seven Blessings, and finds people there praying the Amidah, with no room to distance themselves - it is better for them to quietly recite words of Torah or Psalms by heart rather than sit in silence doing nothing.
takeaways: It is forbidden to sit close (within about two meters) to one praying the Amidah, unless one is engaged in matters of prayer.
One who is forced to sit near someone praying should occupy himself with quiet Torah study or Psalms rather than sit in silence.

paragraphs: Asur laabor betok arba ammot shellipne hammitpallel, abal laachorayv velitzdadin muttar, ulepi dibre zohar haqqadosh lepanayv asur kimlo enayv, velitzdadin velaachorayv asur tok arba ammot davqa, ubevadday shetztzarik lehizzaher kechumrat zohar haqqadosh, ak bishat haddechaq kegon haober holek lehitpallel, o lidbar mitzva vetzarik lemaher, yesh lismok al sebarat maran za"l dela asar ella lepanayv tok arba ammot davqa, vaapillu im yesh mechitztza lipne hammitpallel, bemaqom gabohha asara tepachim verachab arbaa tepachim, gam ken asur laabor lepanayv, vehashshalicha tzibbur apillu eno omed bitpillat shemoneh esreh ella oseq bishar tiqqune hattepilla gam ken asur laabor lepanayv: umeboar besipre haacharonim za"l daapillu im yesh keneged hammitpallel kotel zekukit, tzarik lehizzaher shello yaabor lepanayv, deap al gab dekotel hazzekukit mapsiq mikkol maqom hu roehu utebattel kavvanato:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to pass within four cubits in front of one who is praying, but behind him and to the sides it is permitted. According to the holy Zohar, it is forbidden to pass in front of him even at a greater distance ("as far as his eyes can see"), and to the sides and behind him it is forbidden only within four cubits specifically - and it is proper to be stringent according to the view of the Zohar. However, in a time of pressing need, such as one who is himself going to pray or going for the sake of an urgent mitzvah, one may rely on the view of Maran (the Shulchan Aruch), who forbids only passing in front of him within four cubits. Even if there is a partition ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide in front of the one praying, it is still forbidden to pass in front of him. Likewise, the prayer leader, even when he is not standing in the Amidah itself but in the other parts of the prayer, one may not pass in front of him. Even if there is a glass wall between the one praying and the one passing - it is forbidden to pass in front of him, because the one praying still sees him, and this nullifies his intent.
takeaways: One should not pass within about two meters in front of one who is praying; in a time of pressing need, one may be lenient and pass to the side or behind.
Even a glass partition does not permit passing in front of one who is praying, since he can still see the person passing, which nullifies his intent.

paragraphs: Mi shehishlim tepillato veadam acher odennu mitpallel leacharayv betok arba ammot, lo yaaseh shalosh pesiot ad shezzeh yashlim tepillato, deim posea nimtza hu ober keneged hammitpallel, vetzarik lehizzaher apillu im zeh hammitpallel hitchil bitpillat haamida besop hattepilla shello:

clarification.explanation: One who has finished his prayer, while another person is still praying behind him within four cubits, should not take the three steps (the steps taken at the end of the prayer) until the other one finishes, because otherwise he would end up passing in front of the one praying. One must be careful of this even if the other person only just began his prayer while the one who finished is already at the end of his own prayer.
takeaways: Before taking the three steps at the end of prayer, one must make sure there is no one else praying behind him who might be affected by it.

paragraphs: Yekavven raglayv zeh etzel zeh keillu enam ella echad, veyakop rosho meat sheyyihyu enayv lematta, velo yakop harbeh. velibbo, yekavven lemala lashshamayim, veim mitpallel beal peh yaatzim enayv veyannicha yadayv al libbo keputim hayyemanit al hassemalit, vehaggodelim yihyu lipnim veomed keebed lipne hammelek beema vapachad, veameru bazzohar haqqadosh man depiqqeach enayv betzilluteh maqdim aleha malak hammavet veeno zokeh lirot or shekina betzet napsho beet petirato, veim hukrach liptoach enayv bishbil ezeh sibba hekrechit yishtoq veyiptach enayv vetekep yisgor enayv veyachazor litpillot, veap al pi sheyyoter tob lehitpallel beenayim segurot mikkol maqom im yodea beatzmo sheyyesh lo kavvanat halleb yoter bihyoto mitpallel mittok hassiddur- mitpallel mittok hasseper veraq yizzaher shello yistakkel chutz min hasseper shebbeyado apillu kol dehu, vegam yizzaher kesheoseh hishtachavaya lisgor enayv ap al pi shehasseper beyado, abal bitpilla shel meyushshab matchil parashat haaqeda ad tepillat haamida vadday adip tepe mittok hasseper baabur hakkavvana, vegam kede shello yibla veyashmit tebot o otiyyot, vegam bitpillot dimyushshab yizzaher shello yismok laachorayv velo litzdadin velo yipshot raglayv velo yarkibem zeh al gabbe zeh, ella yesheb beema vekabod vekannizkar baacharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: One should stand with the feet together, one beside the other, as though they were one, and bow the head slightly downward (but not too much), while the heart is directed upward toward Heaven. If praying by heart, it is good to close the eyes and place the hands on the heart interlocked, the right hand over the left, with the thumbs facing outward, and stand like a servant before his king in awe and reverence. The holy Zohar says that one who opens his eyes during his prayer, the Angel of Death hastens to him and he will not merit to see the Divine Presence at the time of his passing. If compelled to open the eyes for some unavoidable reason, one should pause, open them, and immediately close them again and continue praying. Nevertheless, if a person knows that he has better intent when praying from the prayer book - it is preferable that he pray this way from the book, provided he looks at nothing else but the book, and that he closes his eyes during bowing even while holding the book. In the sitting prayer (from the passage of the Akeidah until the Amidah), it is certainly preferable to pray from the book, both to preserve intent and so as not to swallow letters or words. In prayer while sitting, one must also be careful not to lean backward or to the sides, not to stretch out the legs, and not to cross them, but to sit in awe and dignity.
takeaways: It is proper to close the eyes during the Amidah and stand in awe and reverence like a servant before his king, unless one's concentration is better while praying from the prayer book.
Even in prayer while sitting, one should sit with dignity - without leaning, stretching out the legs, or crossing them.

paragraphs: Hacholeh im i epshar lo lehitpallel meummad muttar lehitpallel al yede semika, veim gam zeh lo epshar lo yitpallel meyushshab, vaapillu shokeb al tziddo kede shello lebattel tepilla apillu bechaleyo, vah' yisadennu al eres devay:

clarification.explanation: A sick person who cannot pray standing is permitted to pray while supported by something; and if even that is not possible, he should pray sitting; and even lying on his side, provided that he does not forgo prayer even during his illness - and may Hashem grant him a complete recovery.
takeaways: A sick person who cannot stand for prayer should pray supported, and if that is not possible, sitting, and even lying down - the main point being that he not lose out on prayer.

paragraphs: Kol adam shehu bari asur lismok atzmo bitpillat haamida lakkotel o ledabar acher, vehashshalicha tzibbur ushear bene adam sheddarkam lehitpallel etzel hatteba, yasimu lebabam al amidatam beet tepillat haamida shello yihyu nismakim batteba, ki yesh nismakim velav addatayhu:

clarification.explanation: A healthy person is forbidden to lean during the Amidah on a wall or on anything else. The prayer leader and others accustomed to praying near the prayer stand must pay close attention not to lean on the stand without realizing it.
takeaways: One who is healthy should not lean on anything during the Amidah - and special attention is needed for one accustomed to standing near the prayer stand, that he not be supported by it without noticing.

paragraphs: Keshehu mitpallel tepillat haamida lo yochaz beyado lo tepillin velo seper satum sheeno mitpallel bo, velo shum dabar sheim yippol miyyado yiqsheh alayv, mippene shellibbo yihyeh tarud baaburam, veken name lo yitpallel bemaqom sheyyesh dabar shemmebattel kavvanato kegon qol, debarim vekaddomeh, veyesh machmirim shello yitpallel bebatte enayim im hem repuyim delibbo tarud bahem shello yippolu, veayyen "peri haadama" cheleq  dap t"v ammud d. vetzarik lehizzaher bazeh:

clarification.explanation: During the Amidah one should not hold in the hand either tefillin or a closed book from which one is not praying, nor anything that, if it fell from the hand, would cause distress, because it would occupy the mind. Likewise, one should not pray in a place where there is a disturbance that nullifies concentration, such as noise or conversation. Some are stringent that one should not pray with loose eyeglasses that might fall, since this preoccupies the mind - and one must be careful about this.
takeaways: One should not hold in the hand anything that might fall and distract the mind during prayer, and one should not pray in a place with noise or disturbance.

paragraphs: Hammitpallel mittok siddur venapal miyyado veeno yakol lekavven biladu, muttar lehagbiho achar siyyum habberaka, veken im aqatzo parosh o kinna veeno yakol lisbol shehu mitbalbel baabur zot yemashmesh bibgadayv kede lahasiram, abal lo yesirem beyado, veim yesh tinoq matrido o bene adam medabberim matridim oto, muttar laasot tenua beqol davqa bilti dibbur kede lehashtiqam, veyaasenna achar gemar habberaka:

clarification.explanation: One who is praying from a prayer book, and it falls from his hand, and he cannot continue to concentrate without it, is permitted to pick it up only after finishing the blessing he is in. Likewise, one who is bitten by a flea or louse and cannot bear it, should feel through his clothing to remove it, but should not remove it directly with his hands. If a child disturbs him, or people talking disturb him, he is permitted to make a vocal sound (without speaking) to quiet them, but only after finishing the blessing.
takeaways: Minor disturbances during prayer (a dropped prayer book, an insect bite, noise) are dealt with only at the end of the current blessing, not in the middle of it, and cautiously - without speaking.

paragraphs: Asur lehitpallel neged mareh, apillu enayv segurot demecheze kemishtachaveh lebabua shello, veim yesh tziyyurim bakkotel o bibgadim happerushim kenegdo, im hem boletot asur lehitpallel kenegdan apillu beenayv segurot veim en boletot muttar lehitpallel kenegdan beenayv segurot:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to pray facing a mirror, even when closing the eyes, because it appears as though one is bowing to one's own reflection in the mirror. If there are images on the wall or on garments spread out in front of the one praying - if the images are raised/embossed, it is forbidden to pray facing them even with closed eyes; and if they are not raised, it is permitted to pray facing them with closed eyes.
takeaways: One should never pray facing a mirror, nor facing raised images, even with closed eyes.

paragraphs: Lo yaamod lehitpallel beli beged elyon shellobeshin al hachilluq, o belo ezor, o belo mikseh haelyon shel harosh sheqqorin "piyyes" (migbaat) ap al pi shellobesh mikseh haddaq sheqqorin "rqg'yn" (kippa), zeh hakkelal kol shebbeoto maqom maqpidim lebilti yaamdu lipne gedolim bechesron malbushim ellu vekayyotze bahen, asur lo laamod lipne melek hakkabod bitpilla, vetzarik lehizzaher bazeh anshe ayarenu sheyyesh rabbim mitpallelim arbit beyachid bebetam vegam bimot haqqayitz poshetim begadim elyonim mechamat hachom keshebbaim lebetam tekep, shetztzerikin lehizzaher bazeh beet tepilla, vederek hachakamim sheen mitpallelim ella keshehem atupim biglima hu beged haelyon shehaadam lobesh kesheholek bashshuq ubarechobot, mishshum "hikkon liqrat eloheka yisrael" (amos d, yb), verauy lekol adam lehitnaheg bekak apillu hu hedyot:

clarification.explanation: One should not stand to pray without an outer garment over the undergarment, without a belt, and without an outer head covering (a hat), even if wearing a thin skullcap underneath. The rule is: wherever it is customary to be careful not to stand before important people lacking these garments, it is forbidden to stand this way before the King of kings in prayer. The townspeople who pray the evening service alone at home must be warned, and in summer they remove their outer garment because of the heat when they arrive home - they must be careful about this at the time of prayer. The way of the Sages is to pray specifically while wrapped in an outer garment (a cloak) worn when going out into the street, because of the verse "Prepare to meet your God, Israel," and it is proper for every person to conduct himself this way, even a simple person.
takeaways: One should dress with dignity for prayer - an outer garment, a belt, and a head covering - just as one would dress to stand before an important person.
Even one praying alone at home in the evening, after having changed clothes because of the heat, must take care to wear a suitable outer garment for prayer.

paragraphs: Qodem sheyyitpallel yasir kicho venio vetzoat hachotem al yede beged vekol dabar hattoredo, veasur laroq bihyoto mitpallel tepillat haamida, veim mukrach laroq mishshum demitterid yablia haroq bemitpachat shebbecheqo o biksuto, velo yablia haroq ella ad sheyyishtoq kede hilluk arba ammot vekol shekken keshehu haya mazkir et hashshem, velo yegaheq lirtzono vehu mah sheqqorin bearbi "qecha" (shiul yabesh) ki im mittok ones davqa, veken lo yepaheq lirtzono vehu mah sheqqorin bearbi "titavveb" (pihuq shel tardema), veim hukrach lepaheq shello haya yakol limnoa atzmo, az yishtoq veyannicha yadayv al piv shello titraeh petichato, veap al pi sheomed lebaddo veen sham adam roehu:

clarification.explanation: Before prayer one should remove phlegm, mucus, and nasal discharge with a handkerchief, and anything else that is disturbing. It is forbidden to spit during the Amidah, and if one is compelled to spit because of a disturbance, he should absorb the spit into a handkerchief in his bosom or his garment, and should not do so immediately, but wait an amount of time equivalent to walking four cubits (a short distance), and certainly not while mentioning the Name of Hashem. One should not belch (a dry cough) intentionally, but only if it happens involuntarily; likewise one should not yawn (a yawn of drowsiness) intentionally. If compelled to yawn and unable to prevent it, one should pause and place the hands over the mouth so that its opening is not seen, even if alone with no one watching.
takeaways: Before prayer one should clear phlegm and nasal discharge so as not to be disturbed by it during the prayer itself.
Spitting, coughing, or yawning during prayer should be done only when unavoidable, gently and while covering the mouth - even when no one is watching.

paragraphs: Im mitpallel besiddur sheen tepillat haamida shelema bo bammaqom echad ella tzarik lehitpallel bo mishte meqomot, lo yehapek bedappim bitpillato, ella yetzayyen maqom hashsheni qodem hattepilla bedabar acher kede sheyyitpallel mittoko bilti chippus, utohar yadayim yosip ometz littol yadayv bemayim qodem tepilla velo yaabor, veshammash bet hakkeneset tzarik lehashgicha bedabar zeh lehakin etzel petach bet hakkeneset kelim meleim mayim kede shehaqqahal yittelu yedehem keshebbaim leet mincha min hashshuq lebet hakkeneset, abal beshacharit kol adam notel bebeto uba:

clarification.explanation: One who prays from a prayer book in which the Amidah is not complete in one place, but is divided between two places in the book, should not turn the pages during the prayer itself, but should mark the second place in advance (before the prayer) with some marker, so that he can continue from there without searching. And one of greater devotion (who is particular) should also wash his hands with water before prayer. The synagogue attendant must see to it to prepare vessels full of water near the entrance of the synagogue, so that the congregation can wash their hands when they come from the marketplace for the Mincha prayer; but for the morning prayer, everyone washes at home before coming.
takeaways: One whose prayer book requires flipping pages in the middle of the Amidah should mark the second place in advance so as not to search during the prayer.
It is good to wash the hands before prayer, and the synagogue should prepare water for washing before the Mincha prayer.

paragraphs: Asur leekol velishtot qodem tepillat shacharit, vaapillu bemayim bilbad yesh lehachmir im lo mishshum yishshub haddaat, veken im mukrach lishtot mashqeh sammim shel repua shari, vekevan shehiggia zeman tepilla asur laasoq bitzrakayv ad sheyyitpallel:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to eat or drink before the morning prayer, and even drinking water alone should be treated stringently unless it is necessary for settling the mind. One who is compelled to drink a liquid medicine is permitted to do so. From the moment the time for prayer arrives, a person is forbidden to attend to his personal affairs until he has prayed.
takeaways: One should not eat or drink (except water for settling the mind, or necessary medicine) before the morning prayer.
From the time the prayer's time arrives, one must pray first, and not occupy himself with mundane matters.

paragraphs: Mi shehaya bassadeh vehiggia zeman tepilla demukrach lehitpallel sham, yishtaddel lehitpallel bemaqom tzanua dehaynu ben hailanot heka deepshar, veim yesh sham maqom muqqap mechitztzot yikkanes lehitpallel sham, ubilbad sheyyihyeh hammaqom naqi demeachar shehu muqqap mechitztzot ap al pi sheen sham tiqra chashib maqom tzanua, umah deasur lehitpallel bebaqeta hu mishshum deen sham mechitztzot kelal, veayyen "birke yosep" za"l mah shekkatab beshem harab "batte kehunna" za"l veayyen "minchat aharon" kelal t"v ot ch ayyen sham, upoh irenu y" hamminhag lehitpallel baqqayitz rob hatztzibbur bemaqom sheen bo tiqra, veyesh batte kenesiyyot mitpallelim rob yemot hashshana al gag bet hakkeneset kamma kittot:

clarification.explanation: One who is in a field and the time for prayer arrives, such that he is compelled to pray there, should try to find a modest place, such as among the trees, if possible. If there is a place there surrounded by partitions, he should enter to pray there, provided the place is clean, because even without a roof, a place surrounded by partitions is considered a modest place. The prohibition against praying in an open shed [bakta] applies specifically when there are no partitions there at all. Rabbi Yosef Chaim adds that in his city it is customary in summer for most of the congregation to pray in a place without a roof, and there are synagogues where they pray most of the year on the synagogue roof, in several groups.
takeaways: One praying in an open area should seek a modest place (among trees, or a place surrounded by partitions) even if it has no roof.
A place with no partitions at all (such as an open shed) is unfit for prayer, but a place surrounded by partitions without a roof is fit.
